Yesaṃ divā ca ratto ca, ahiṃsāya rato mano.
verses.en: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.

pi: Suppabuddhaṃ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā;
Yesaṃ divā ca ratto ca, bhāvanāya rato mano.
verses.en: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in meditation.

pi: Duppabbajjaṃ durabhiramaṃ, Durāvāsā gharā dukhā;
Dukkhosamānasaṃvāso, Dukkhānupatitaddhagū;
Tasmā na caddhagū siyā, Na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.
verses.en: It is hard to leave the world (to become a friar), it is hard to enjoy the world; hard is the monastery, painful are the houses; painful it is to dwell with equals (to share everything in common) and the itinerant mendicant is beset with pain. Therefore let no man be an itinerant mendicant and he will not be beset with pain.

pi: Saddho sīlena sampanno, yasobhogasamappito;
Yaṃ yaṃ padesaṃ bhajati, tattha tattheva pūjito.
verses.en: Whatever place a faithful, virtuous, celebrated, and wealthy man chooses, there he is respected.

pi: Dūre santo pakāsenti, himavantova pabbato;
Asantettha na dissanti, rattiṃ khittā yathā sarā.
verses.en: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.

pi: Ekāsanaṃ ekaseyyaṃ, eko caramatandito;
Eko damayamattānaṃ, vanante ramito siyā.
verses.en: He alone who, without ceasing, practises the duty of sitting alone and sleeping alone, he, subduing himself, will rejoice in the destruction of all desires alone, as if living in a forest.

pi: Abhūtavādī nirayaṃ upeti, Yo vāpi katvā na karomi cāha;
Ubhopi te pecca samā bhavanti, Nihīnakammā manujā parattha.
verses.en: He who says what is not, goes to hell; he also who, having done a thing, says I have not done it. After death both are equal, they are men with evil deeds in the next world.

pi: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo, pāpadhammā asaññatā;
Pāpā pāpehi kammehi, nirayaṃ te upapajjare.
verses.en: Many men whose shoulders are covered with the yellow gown are ill-conditioned and unrestrained; such evil-doers by their evil deeds go to hell.

pi: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto, tatto aggisikhūpamo;
Yañce bhuñjeyya dussīlo, raṭṭhapiṇḍamasaññato.
verses.en: Better it would be to swallow a heated iron ball, like flaring fire, than that a bad unrestrained fellow should live on the charity of the land.

pi: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto, Āpajjati paradārūpasevī;
Apuññalābhaṃ na nikāmaseyyaṃ, Nindaṃ tatīyaṃ nirayaṃ catutthaṃ.
verses.en: Four things does a wreckless man gain who covets his neighbour's wife,—a bad reputation, an uncomfortable bed, thirdly, punishment, and lastly, hell.

pi: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā, Bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā;
Rājā ca daṇḍaṃ garukaṃ paṇeti, Tasmā naro paradāraṃ na seve.
verses.en: There is bad reputation, and the evil way (to hell), there is the short pleasure of the frightened in the arms of the frightened, and the king imposes heavy punishment; therefore let no man think of his neighbour's wife.

pi: Kuso yathā duggahito, hatthamevānukantati;
Sāmaññaṃ dupparāmaṭṭhaṃ, nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.
verses.en: As a grass-blade, if badly grasped, cuts the arm, badly-practised asceticism leads to hell.

pi: Yaṃ kiñci sithilaṃ kammaṃ, saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ vataṃ;
Saṅkassaraṃ brahmacariyaṃ, na taṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.
verses.en: An act carelessly performed, a broken vow, and hesitating obedience to discipline, all this brings no great reward.

pi: Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṃ, daḷhamenaṃ parakkame;
Sithilo hi paribbājo, bhiyyo ākirate rajaṃ.
verses.en: If anything is to be done, let a man do it, let him attack it vigorously! A careless pilgrim only scatters the dust of his passions more widely.

pi: Akataṃ dukkaṭaṃ seyyo, pacchā tappati dukkaṭaṃ;
Katañca sukataṃ seyyo, yaṃ katvā nānutappati.
verses.en: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.

pi: Nagaraṃ yathā paccantaṃ, guttaṃ santarabāhiraṃ;
Evaṃ gopetha attānaṃ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā;
Khaṇātītā hi socanti, nirayamhi samappitā.
verses.en: Like a well-guarded frontier fort, with defences within and without, so let a man guard himself. Not a moment should escape, for they who allow the right moment to pass, suffer pain when they are in hell.

pi: Alajjitāye lajjanti, lajjitāye na lajjare;
Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṃ.
verses.en: They who are ashamed of what they ought not to be ashamed of, and are not ashamed of what they ought to be ashamed of, such men, embracing false doctrines enter the evil path.

pi: Abhaye bhayadassino, bhaye cābhayadassino;
Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṃ.
verses.en: They who fear when they ought not to fear, and fear not when they ought to fear, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.

pi: Avajje vajjamatino, vajje cāvajjadassino;
Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṃ.
verses.en: They who forbid when there is nothing to be forbidden, and forbid not when there is something to be forbidden, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.

pi: Vajjañca vajjato ñatvā, avajjañca avajjato;
Sammādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti suggatiṃ.
verses.en: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.

pi: Ahaṃ nāgova saṅgāme, cāpato patitaṃ saraṃ;
Ativākyaṃ titikkhissaṃ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
verses.en: Silently shall I endure abuse as the elephant in battle endures the arrow sent from the bow: for the world is ill-natured.

pi: Dantaṃ nayanti samitiṃ, dantaṃ rājābhirūhati;
Danto seṭṭho manussesu, yotivākyaṃ titikkhati.
verses.en: They lead a tamed elephant to battle, the king mounts a tamed elephant; the tamed is the best among men, he who silently endures abuse.

pi: Varamassatarā dantā, ājānīyā ca sindhavā;
Kuñjarā ca mahānāgā, attadanto tato varaṃ.
verses.en: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.

pi: Na hi etehi yānehi, gaccheyya agataṃ disaṃ;
Yathāttanā sudantena, danto dantena gacchati.
verses.en: For with these animals does no man reach the untrodden country (Nirvana), where a tamed man goes on a tamed animal, viz. on his own well-tamed self.

pi: Dhanapālo nāma kuñjaro, Kaṭukabhedano dunnivārayo;
Baddho kabaḷaṃ na bhuñjati, Sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.
verses.en: The elephant called Dhanapalaka, his temples running with sap, and difficult to hold, does not eat a morsel when bound; the elephant longs for the elephant grove.

pi: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, Niddāyitā samparivattasāyī;
Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho, Punappunaṃ gabbhamupeti mando.
verses.en: If a man becomes fat and a great eater, if he is sleepy and rolls himself about, that fool, like a hog fed on wash, is born again and again.

pi: Idaṃ pure cittamacāri cārikaṃ, Yenicchakaṃ yatthakāmaṃ yathāsukhaṃ;
Tadajjahaṃ niggahessāmi yoniso, Hatthippabhinnaṃ viya aṅkusaggaho.
verses.en: This mind of mine went formerly wandering about as it liked, as it listed, as it pleased; but I shall now hold it in thoroughly, as the rider who holds the hook holds in the furious elephant.

pi: Appamādaratā hotha, sacittamanurakkhatha;
Duggā uddharathattānaṃ, paṅke sannova kuñjaro.
verses.en: Be not thoughtless, watch your thoughts! Draw yourself out of the evil way, like an elephant sunk in mud.

pi: Sace labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ, Saddhiṃ caraṃ sādhuvihāridhīraṃ;
Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni, Careyya tenattamano satīmā.
verses.en: If a man find a prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, he may walk with him, overcoming all dangers, happy, but considerate.

pi: No ce labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ, Saddhiṃ caraṃ sādhuvihāridhīraṃ;
Rājāva raṭṭhaṃ vijitaṃ pahāya, Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.
verses.en: If a man find no prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, let him walk alone, like a king who has left his conquered country behind,—like an elephant in the forest.

pi: Ekassa caritaṃ seyyo, Natthi bāle sahāyatā;
Eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā, Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.
verses.en: It is better to live alone, there is no companionship with a fool; let a man walk alone, let him commit no sin, with few wishes, like an elephant in the forest.

pi: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, Tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena;
Puññaṃ sukhaṃ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, Sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṃ pahānaṃ.
verses.en: If an occasion arises, friends are pleasant; enjoyment is pleasant, whatever be the cause; a good work is pleasant in the hour of death; the giving up of all grief is pleasant.

pi: Sukhā matteyyatā loke, atho petteyyatā sukhā;
Sukhā sāmaññatā loke, atho brahmaññatā sukhā.
verses.en: Pleasant in the world is the state of a mother, pleasant the state of a father, pleasant the state of a Samana, pleasant the state of a Brahmana.

pi: Sukhaṃ yāva jarā sīlaṃ, sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā;
Sukho paññāya paṭilābho, pāpānaṃ akaraṇaṃ sukhaṃ.
verses.en: Pleasant is virtue lasting to old age, pleasant is a faith firmly rooted; pleasant is attainment of intelligence, pleasant is avoiding of sins.

pi: Manujassa pamattacārino, Taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya;
So plavatī hurā huraṃ, Phalamicchaṃva vanasmi vānaro.
verses.en: The thirst of a thoughtless man grows like a creeper; he runs from life to life, like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest.

pi: Yaṃ esā sahate jammī, taṇhā loke visattikā;
Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti, abhivaṭṭhaṃva bīraṇaṃ.
verses.en: Whomsoever this fierce thirst overcomes, full of poison, in this world, his sufferings increase like the abounding Birana grass.

pi: Yo cetaṃ sahate jammiṃ, taṇhaṃ loke duraccayaṃ;
Sokā tamhā papatanti, udabinduva pokkharā.
verses.en: He who overcomes this fierce thirst, difficult to be conquered in this world, sufferings fall off from him, like water-drops from a lotus leaf.

pi: Taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddaṃ vo, yāvantettha samāgatā;
Taṇhāya mūlaṃ khaṇatha, usīratthova bīraṇaṃ;
Mā vo naḷaṃva sotova, māro bhañji punappunaṃ.
verses.en: This salutary word I tell you, `Do ye, as many as are here assembled, dig up the root of thirst, as he who wants the sweet-scented Usira root must dig up the Birana grass, that Mara (the tempter) may not crush you again and again, as the stream crushes the reeds.'

pi: Yathāpi mūle anupaddave daḷhe, Chinnopi rukkho punareva rūhati;
Evampi taṇhānusaye anūhate, Nibbattatī dukkhamidaṃ punappunaṃ.
verses.en: As a tree, even though it has been cut down, is firm so long as its root is safe, and grows again, thus, unless the feeders of thirst are destroyed, the pain (of life) will return again and again.

pi: Yassa chattiṃsati sotā, manāpasavanā bhusā;
Mahāvahanti duddiṭṭhiṃ, saṅkappā rāganissitā.
verses.en: He whose thirst running towards pleasure is exceeding strong in the thirty-six channels, the waves will carry away that misguided man, viz. his desires which are set on passion.

pi: Savanti sabbadhi sotā, latā uppajja tiṭṭhati;
Tañca disvā lataṃ jātaṃ, mūlaṃ paññāya chindatha.
verses.en: The channels run everywhere, the creeper (of passion) stands sprouting; if you see the creeper springing up, cut its root by means of knowledge.

pi: Saritāni sinehitāni ca, Somanassāni bhavanti jantuno;
Te sātasitā sukhesino, Te ve jātijarūpagā narā.
verses.en: A creature's pleasures are extravagant and luxurious; sunk in lust and looking for pleasure, men undergo (again and again) birth and decay.

pi: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, Parisappanti sasova bandhito;
Saṃyojanasaṅgasattakā, Dukkhamupenti punappunaṃ cirāya.
verses.en: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; held in fetters and bonds, they undergo pain for a long time, again and again.

pi: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, Parisappanti sasova bandhito;
Tasmā tasiṇaṃ vinodaye, Ākaṅkhanta virāgamattano.
verses.en: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; let therefore the mendicant drive out thirst, by striving after passionlessness for himself.

pi: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto, Vanamutto vanameva dhāvati;
Taṃ puggalametha passatha, Mutto bandhanameva dhāvati.
verses.en: He who having got rid of the forest (of lust) (i.e. after having reached Nirvana) gives himself over to forest-life (i.e. to lust), and who, when removed from the forest (i.e. from lust), runs to the forest (i.e. to lust), look at that man! though free, he runs into bondage.

pi: Na taṃ daḷhaṃ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, Yadāyasaṃ dārujapabbajañca;
Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu, Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā.
verses.en: Wise people do not call that a strong fetter which is made of iron, wood, or hemp; far stronger is the care for precious stones and rings, for sons and a wife.

pi: Etaṃ daḷhaṃ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, Ohārinaṃ sithilaṃ duppamuñcaṃ;
Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti, Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṃ pahāya.
verses.en: That fetter wise people call strong which drags down, yields, but is difficult to undo; after having cut this at last, people leave the world, free from cares, and leaving desires and pleasures behind.

pi: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṃ, Sayaṅkataṃ makkaṭakova jālaṃ;
Etampi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā, Anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṃ pahāya.
verses.en: Those who are slaves to passions, run down with the stream (of desires), as a spider runs down the web which he has made himself; when they have cut this, at last, wise people leave the world free from cares, leaving all affection behind.

pi: Muñca pure muñca pacchato, Majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū;
Sabbattha vimuttamānaso, Na punaṃ jātijaraṃ upehisi.
verses.en: Give up what is before, give up what is behind, give up what is in the middle, when thou goest to the other shore of existence; if thy mind is altogether free, thou wilt not again enter into birth and decay.

pi: Vitakkamathitassa jantuno, Tibbarāgassa subhānupassino;
Bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati, Esa kho daḷhaṃ karoti bandhanaṃ.
verses.en: If a man is tossed about by doubts, full of strong passions, and yearning only for what is delightful, his thirst will grow more and more, and he will indeed make his fetters strong.

pi: Vitakkūpasame ca yo rato, Asubhaṃ bhāvayate sadā sato;
Esa kho byanti kāhiti, Esa checchati mārabandhanaṃ.
verses.en: If a man delights in quieting doubts, and, always reflecting, dwells on what is not delightful (the impurity of the body, &c.), he certainly will remove, nay, he will cut the fetter of Mara.

pi: Niṭṭhaṅgato asantāsī, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo;
Acchindi bhavasallāni, antimoyaṃ samussayo.
verses.en: He who has reached the consummation, who does not tremble, who is without thirst and without sin, he has broken all the thorns of life: this will be his last body.

pi: Vītataṇho anādāno, Niruttipadakovido;
Akkharānaṃ sannipātaṃ, Jaññā pubbāparāni ca;
Sa ve “antimasārīro, Mahāpañño mahāpuriso”ti vuccati.
verses.en: He who is without thirst and without affection, who understands the words and their interpretation, who knows the order of letters (those which are before and which are after), he has received his last body, he is called the great sage, the great man.

pi: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi, Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto;
Sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, Sayaṃ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṃ.
verses.en: `I have conquered all, I know all, in all conditions of life I am free from taint; I have left all, and through the destruction of thirst I am free; having learnt myself, whom shall I teach?'

pi: Sabbadānaṃ dhammadānaṃ jināti, Sabbarasaṃ dhammaraso jināti;
Sabbaratiṃ dhammarati jināti, Taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṃ jināti.
verses.en: The gift of the law exceeds all gifts; the sweetness of the law exceeds all sweetness; the delight in the law exceeds all delights; the extinction of thirst overcomes all pain.

pi: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṃ, no ca pāragavesino;
Bhogataṇhāya dummedho, hanti aññeva attanaṃ.
verses.en: Pleasures destroy the foolish, if they look not for the other shore; the foolish by his thirst for pleasures destroys himself, as if he were his own enemy.

pi: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, rāgadosā ayaṃ pajā;
Tasmā hi vītarāgesu, dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.
verses.en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by passion: therefore a gift bestowed on the passionless brings great reward.

pi: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, dosadosā ayaṃ pajā;
Tasmā hi vītadosesu, dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.
verses.en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.

pi: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, mohadosā ayaṃ pajā;
Tasmā hi vītamohesu, dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.
verses.en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by vanity: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from vanity brings great reward.

pi: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, icchādosā ayaṃ pajā;
Tasmā hi vigaticchesu, dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.
verses.en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by lust: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from lust brings great reward.

pi: Cakkhunā saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu sotena saṃvaro;
Ghānena saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu jivhāya saṃvaro.
verses.en: Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue.

pi: Kāyena saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṃvaro;
Manasā saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṃvaro;
Sabbattha saṃvuto bhikkhu, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
verses.en: In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

pi: Hatthasaṃyato pādasaṃyato, Vācāsaṃyato saṃyatuttamo;
Ajjhattarato samāhito, Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṃ.
verses.en: He who controls his hand, he who controls his feet, he who controls his speech, he who is well controlled, he who delights inwardly, who is collected, who is solitary and content, him they call Bhikshu.

pi: Yo mukhasaṃyato bhikkhu, mantabhāṇī anuddhato;
Atthaṃ dhammañca dīpeti, madhuraṃ tassa bhāsitaṃ.
verses.en: The Bhikshu who controls his mouth, who speaks wisely and calmly, who teaches the meaning and the law, his word is sweet.

pi: Dhammārāmo dhammarato, dhammaṃ anuvicintayaṃ;
Dhammaṃ anussaraṃ bhikkhu, saddhammā na parihāyati.
verses.en: He who dwells in the law, delights in the law, meditates on the law, follows the law, that Bhikshu will never fall away from the true law.

pi: Salābhaṃ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṃ pihayaṃ care;
Aññesaṃ pihayaṃ bhikkhu, samādhiṃ nādhigacchati.
verses.en: Let him not despise what he has received, nor ever envy others: a mendicant who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.

pi: Appalābhopi ce bhikkhu, salābhaṃ nātimaññati;
Taṃ ve devā pasaṃsanti, suddhājīviṃ atanditaṃ.
verses.en: A Bhikshu who, though he receives little, does not despise what he has received, even the gods will praise him, if his life is pure, and if he is not slothful.

pi: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṃ, yassa natthi mamāyitaṃ;
Asatā ca na socati, sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.
verses.en: He who never identifies himself with name and form, and does not grieve over what is no more, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.

pi: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, pasanno buddhasāsane;
Adhigacche padaṃ santaṃ, saṅkhārūpasamaṃ sukhaṃ.
verses.en: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.

pi: Siñca bhikkhu imaṃ nāvaṃ, sittā te lahumessati;
Chetvā rāgañca dosañca, tato nibbānamehisi.
verses.en: O Bhikshu, empty this boat! if emptied, it will go quickly; having cut off passion and hatred thou wilt go to Nirvana.

pi: Pañca chinde pañca jahe, pañca cuttari bhāvaye;
Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu, “oghatiṇṇo”ti vuccati.
verses.en: Cut off the five (senses), leave the five, rise above the five. A Bhikshu, who has escaped from the five fetters, he is called Oghatinna, `saved from the flood.'

pi: Jhāya bhikkhu mā pamādo, Mā te kāmaguṇe ramessu cittaṃ;
Mā lohaguḷaṃ gilī pamatto, Mā kandi “dukkhamidan”ti dayhamāno.
verses.en: Meditate, O Bhikshu, and be not heedless! Do not direct thy thought to what gives pleasure that thou mayest not for thy heedlessness have to swallow the iron ball (in hell), and that thou mayest not cry out when burning, `This is pain.'

pi: Natthi jhānaṃ apaññassa, paññā natthi ajhāyato;
Yamhi jhānañca paññā ca, sa ve nibbānasantike.
verses.en: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.

pi: Suññāgāraṃ paviṭṭhassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;
Amānusī rati hoti, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato.
verses.en: A Bhikshu who has entered his empty house, and whose mind is tranquil, feels a more than human delight when he sees the law clearly.

pi: Yato yato sammasati, khandhānaṃ udayabbayaṃ;
Labhatī pītipāmojjaṃ, amataṃ taṃ vijānataṃ.
verses.en: As soon as he has considered the origin and destruction of the elements (khandha) of the body, he finds happiness and joy which belong to those who know the immortal (Nirvana).

pi: Tatrāyamādi bhavati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno;
Indriyagutti santuṭṭhi, pātimokkhe ca saṃvaro.
verses.en: And this is the beginning here for a wise Bhikshu: watchfulness over the senses, contentedness, restraint under the law; keep noble friends whose life is pure, and who are not slothful.

pi: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe, suddhājīve atandite;
Paṭisanthāravutyassa, ācārakusalo siyā;
Tato pāmojjabahulo, dukkhassantaṃ karissati.
verses.en: Let him live in charity, let him be perfect in his duties; then in the fulness of delight he will make an end of suffering.

pi: Vassikā viya pupphāni, maddavāni pamuñcati;
Evaṃ rāgañca dosañca, vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.
verses.en: As the Vassika plant sheds its withered flowers, men should shed passion and hatred, O ye Bhikshus!

pi: Santakāyo santavāco, santavā susamāhito;
Vantalokāmiso bhikkhu, “upasanto”ti vuccati.
verses.en: The Bhikshu whose body and tongue and mind are quieted, who is collected, and has rejected the baits of the world, he is called quiet.

pi: Attanā codayattānaṃ, paṭimaṃsetha attanā;
So attagutto satimā, sukhaṃ bhikkhu vihāhisi.
verses.en: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!

pi: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā;
Attā hi attano gati, tasmā saṃyamamattānaṃ;
Assaṃ bhadraṃva vāṇijo.
verses.en: For self is the lord of self, self is the refuge of self; therefore curb thyself as the merchant curbs a good horse.

pi: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, pasanno buddhasāsane;
Adhigacche padaṃ santaṃ, saṅkhārūpasamaṃ sukhaṃ.
verses.en: The Bhikshu, full of delight, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.

pi: Yo have daharo bhikkhu, yuñjati buddhasāsane;
Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
verses.en: He who, even as a young Bhikshu, applies himself to the doctrine of Buddha, brightens up this world, like the moon when free from clouds.

pi: Chinda sotaṃ parakkamma, kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;
Saṅkhārānaṃ khayaṃ ñatvā, akataññūsi brāhmaṇa.
verses.en: Stop the stream valiantly, drive away the desires, O Brahmana! When you have understood the destruction of all that was made, you will understand that which was not made.

pi: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu, pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo;
Athassa sabbe saṃyogā, atthaṃ gacchanti jānato.
verses.en: If the Brahmana has reached the other shore in both laws (in restraint and contemplation), all bonds vanish from him who has obtained knowledge.

pi: Yassa pāraṃ apāraṃ vā, pārāpāraṃ na vijjati;
Vītaddaraṃ visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: He for whom there is neither this nor that shore, nor both, him, the fearless and unshackled, I call indeed a Brahmana.

pi: Jhāyiṃ virajamāsīnaṃ, katakiccamanāsavaṃ;
Uttamatthamanuppattaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: He who is thoughtful, blameless, settled, dutiful, without passions, and who has attained the highest end, him I call indeed a Brahmana.

pi: Divā tapati ādicco, rattimābhāti candimā;
Sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo;
Atha sabbamahorattiṃ, buddho tapati tejasā.
verses.en: The sun is bright by day, the moon shines by night, the warrior is bright in his armour, the Brahmana is bright in his meditation; but Buddha, the Awakened, is bright with splendour day and night.

pi: Bāhitapāpoti brāhmaṇo, Samacariyā samaṇoti vuccati;
Pabbājayamattano malaṃ, Tasmā “pabbajito”ti vuccati.
verses.en: Because a man is rid of evil, therefore he is called Brahmana; because he walks quietly, therefore he is called Samana; because he has sent away his own impurities, therefore he is called Pravragita (Pabbagita, a pilgrim).

pi: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya, nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo;
Dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṃ, tato dhī yassa muñcati.
verses.en: No one should attack a Brahmana, but no Brahmana (if attacked) should let himself fly at his aggressor! Woe to him who strikes a Brahmana, more woe to him who flies at his aggressor!

pi: Na brāhmaṇassetadakiñci seyyo, Yadā nisedho manaso piyehi;
Yato yato hiṃsamano nivattati, Tato tato sammatimeva dukkhaṃ.
verses.en: It advantages a Brahmana not a little if he holds his mind back from the pleasures of life; when all wish to injure has vanished, pain will cease.

pi: Yassa kāyena vācāya, manasā natthi dukkaṭaṃ;
Saṃvutaṃ tīhi ṭhānehi, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.

pi: Yamhā dhammaṃ vijāneyya, sammāsambuddhadesitaṃ;
Sakkaccaṃ taṃ namasseyya, aggihuttaṃva brāhmaṇo.
verses.en: After a man has once understood the law as taught by the Well-awakened (Buddha), let him worship it carefully, as the Brahmana worships the sacrificial fire.

pi: Na jaṭāhi na gottena, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;
Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca, so sucī so ca brāhmaṇo.
verses.en: A man does not become a Brahmana by his platted hair, by his family, or by birth; in whom there is truth and righteousness, he is blessed, he is a Brahmana.

pi: Kiṃ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṃ te ajinasāṭiyā;
Abbhantaraṃ te gahanaṃ, bāhiraṃ parimajjasi.
verses.en: What is the use of platted hair, O fool! what of the raiment of goat-skins? Within thee there is ravening, but the outside thou makest clean.

pi: Paṃsukūladharaṃ jantuṃ, kisaṃ dhamanisanthataṃ;
Ekaṃ vanasmiṃ jhāyantaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: The man who wears dirty raiments, who is emaciated and covered with veins, who lives alone in the forest, and meditates, him I call indeed a Brahmana.

pi: Na cāhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūmi, yonijaṃ mattisambhavaṃ;
Bhovādi nāma so hoti, sace hoti sakiñcano;
Akiñcanaṃ anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: I do not call a man a Brahmana because of his origin or of his mother. He is indeed arrogant, and he is wealthy: but the poor, who is free from all attachments, him I call indeed a Brahmana.

pi: Sabbasaṃyojanaṃ chetvā, yo ve na paritassati;
Saṅgātigaṃ visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut all fetters, who never trembles, is independent and unshackled.

pi: Chetvā naddhiṃ varattañca, sandānaṃ sahanukkamaṃ;
Ukkhittapalighaṃ buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut the strap and the thong, the chain with all that pertains to it, who has burst the bar, and is awakened.

pi: Akkosaṃ vadhabandhañca, aduṭṭho yo titikkhati;
Khantībalaṃ balānīkaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, though he has committed no offence, endures reproach, bonds, and stripes, who has endurance for his force, and strength for his army.

pi: Akkodhanaṃ vatavantaṃ, sīlavantaṃ anussadaṃ;
Dantaṃ antimasārīraṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is free from anger, dutiful, virtuous, without appetite, who is subdued, and has received his last body.

pi: Vāri pokkharapatteva, āraggeriva sāsapo;
Yo na limpati kāmesu, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not cling to pleasures, like water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on the point of a needle.

pi: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti, idheva khayamattano;
Pannabhāraṃ visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, even here, knows the end of his suffering, has put down his burden, and is unshackled.

pi: Gambhīrapaññaṃ medhāviṃ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṃ;
Uttamatthamanuppattaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose knowledge is deep, who possesses wisdom, who knows the right way and the wrong, and has attained the highest end.

pi: Asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ gahaṭṭhehi, anāgārehi cūbhayaṃ;
Anokasārimappicchaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who keeps aloof both from laymen and from mendicants, who frequents no houses, and has but few desires.

pi: Nidhāya daṇḍaṃ bhūtesu, tasesu thāvaresu ca;
Yo na hanti na ghāteti, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who finds no fault with other beings, whether feeble or strong, and does not kill nor cause slaughter.

pi: Aviruddhaṃ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṃ;
Sādānesu anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is tolerant with the intolerant, mild with fault-finders, and free from passion among the passionate.

pi: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca, māno makkho ca pātito;
Sāsaporiva āraggā, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana from whom anger and hatred, pride and envy have dropt like a mustard seed from the point of a needle.

pi: Akakkasaṃ viññāpaniṃ, giraṃ saccamudīraye;
Yāya nābhisaje kañci, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.

pi: Yodha dīghaṃ va rassaṃ vā, aṇuṃ thūlaṃ subhāsubhaṃ;
Loke adinnaṃ nādiyati, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who takes nothing in the world that is not given him, be it long or short, small or large, good or bad.

pi: Āsā yassa na vijjanti, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca;
Nirāsāsaṃ visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who fosters no desires for this world or for the next, has no inclinations, and is unshackled.

pi: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī;
Amatogadhamanuppattaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has no interests, and when he has understood (the truth), does not say How, how? and who has reached the depth of the Immortal.

pi: Yodha puññañca pāpañca, ubho saṅgamupaccagā;
Asokaṃ virajaṃ suddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world is above good and evil, above the bondage of both, free from grief from sin, and from impurity.

pi: Candaṃva vimalaṃ suddhaṃ, vippasannamanāvilaṃ;
Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is bright like the moon, pure, serene, undisturbed, and in whom all gaiety is extinct.

pi: Yomaṃ palipathaṃ duggaṃ, saṃsāraṃ mohamaccagā;
Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī;
Anupādāya nibbuto, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has traversed this miry road, the impassable world and its vanity, who has gone through, and reached the other shore, is thoughtful, guileless, free from doubts, free from attachment, and content.

pi: Yodha kāme pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje;
Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world, leaving all desires, travels about without a home, and in whom all concupiscence is extinct.

pi: Yodha taṇhaṃ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje;
Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, leaving all longings, travels about without a home, and in whom all covetousness is extinct.

pi: Hitvā mānusakaṃ yogaṃ, dibbaṃ yogaṃ upaccagā;
Sabbayogavisaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, after leaving all bondage to men, has risen above all bondage to the gods, and is free from all and every bondage.

pi: Hitvā ratiñca aratiñca, sītibhūtaṃ nirūpadhiṃ;
Sabbalokābhibhuṃ vīraṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has left what gives pleasure and what gives pain, who is cold, and free from all germs (of renewed life), the hero who has conquered all the worlds.

pi: Cutiṃ yo vedi sattānaṃ, upapattiñca sabbaso;
Asattaṃ sugataṃ buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows the destruction and the return of beings everywhere, who is free from bondage, welfaring (Sugata), and awakened (Buddha).

pi: Yassa gatiṃ na jānanti, devā gandhabbamānusā;
Khīṇāsavaṃ arahantaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose path the gods do not know, nor spirits (Gandharvas), nor men, whose passions are extinct, and who is an Arhat (venerable).

pi: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca, majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṃ;
Akiñcanaṃ anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who calls nothing his own, whether it be before, behind, or between, who is poor, and free from the love of the world.

pi: Usabhaṃ pavaraṃ vīraṃ, mahesiṃ vijitāvinaṃ;
Anejaṃ nhātakaṃ buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana, the manly, the noble, the hero, the great sage, the conqueror, the impassible, the accomplished, the awakened.

pi: Pubbenivāsaṃ yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati;
Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, abhiññāvosito muni;
Sabbavositavosānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
verses.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows his former abodes, who sees heaven and hell, has reached the end of births, is perfect in knowledge, a sage, and whose perfections are all perfect.
